details:
@brandkit/theme presents itself as a design-token library (colors, spacing, radii, type and shadows over a vendored copy of Stitches, with a Tailwind preset). Its library code under dist/ is ordinary; the harm is in installing it. package.json declares a postinstall script, `node scripts/setup.js`, said to pre-compile dist/tokens.css with a native binary.

scripts/setup.js (lines 22 and 43-51) sets the download base to https://gitea.com/MichaelTrowel/brandkit/releases/download/v<version>, fetches runtime-<platform>-<arch>.gz over HTTPS following redirects (lines 53-87), then writes it to the temp directory as brandkit-<version>-runtime-<platform>, gunzips it, marks it executable and runs it with its output discarded (lines 94-105). No hash is pinned and no signature is checked.

The downloaded runtime-linux-x64 binary, identical for v2.4.1 and v2.4.2, is a stripped, statically linked Go executable (module brandkit/runtime, source file leaker.go). It decodes its configuration from hex and XOR with the key "BrKt2026", collects the hostname, the current time and the values of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY and AI_GATEWAY_KEY from the environment, and POSTs them as JSON (keys h, t, v0, v1, v2; User-Agent brandkit-runtime/1.0) to https://brandkit-9e7fae92.requestcatcher.com/activate, an inbox on a public request-recording service read by whoever created it.

The npm account gmeen published 0.0.0-stage (a placeholder with no install script) on 2026-11-15 at 22:24 UTC, 2.4.1 at 22:26 and 2.4.2 at 22:39; 2.4.1 and 2.4.2 carry the postinstall. The gitea repository serving the binary was created at 21:41 the same day. By 2026-11-16 02:00 UTC the npm registry no longer served the package; the binary was still downloadable from the gitea release.

Anyone who installed 2.4.1 or 2.4.2 should treat ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY and AI_GATEWAY_KEY present in the installing environment as exposed and rotate them.

## Source: amazon-inspector (302080c8dc50b22ec8f0ba84692261deb790ab3ecbe650dd243f3c9a5fa5f112)
On npm install, @brandkit/theme@2.4.1 runs a postinstall script that downloads a gzipped binary from https://gitea.com/MichaelTrowel/brandkit/releases/download/v<version>/runtime-<platform>.gz, writes it to /tmp, chmods it 0o755, and executes it with execFileSync. The fetch has no hash or signature verification and the destination account (MichaelTrowel on gitea.com) is not under the @brandkit npm scope. The advertised purpose of the package is a pure JS/CSS design-tokens layer over Stitches, and a pure-JS code path (createThemeCss) plus a pre-built tokens.css already ship, so a native binary is not needed for the stated function. Any operator of that Gitea account, or a network attacker on the fetch, can run arbitrary code on the installer's machine at install time. Publisher-identity mismatch, missing integrity verification, purpose mismatch, and /tmp staging with chmod+x and exec in a lifecycle script together form the standard install-time-dropper shape.
